edinburgh.leadLine: Smartwatches and symptom tracking in ENDO1000
edinburgh.reason: ENDO1000 combines wearable measurements with repeated symptom reports. That makes this team a concrete place to explore independent validation of WombWise's wearable signals.
edinburgh.ask: Ask whether a separately agreed validation study could compare WombWise's signals with longitudinal symptom measures. ENDO1000 already has its own app; establish what collaboration could add.

oxford.leadLine: Prospective pain-outcome research and an enquiry desk
oxford.reason: Oxford's registered study follows pain outcomes around endometriosis surgery. Its research centre also publishes a general enquiry route, so there is a clear starting point for a validation discussion.
oxford.ask: Ask the EndoCaRe team whether passive wearable measures would answer a useful question alongside their existing pain-outcome research.

birmingham.leadLine: PCOS phenotyping and a business collaboration team
birmingham.reason: DAISy-PCOS brings together clinical phenotyping and metabolic measurements. Birmingham publishes a business route for collaborative research, which could connect WombWise to the relevant PCOS investigators.
birmingham.ask: Ask the business engagement team for an introduction to PCOS researchers interested in evaluating wearable signals alongside clinical phenotyping.

chelsea.leadLine: Endometriosis studies with a verified NHS research route
chelsea.reason: The Trust appears in recent endometriosis study records. Its research office explicitly supports outside researchers and sponsors with feasibility and study setup.
chelsea.ask: Ask Research & Development to route a short wearable-validation proposal to the endometriosis team and clarify the feasibility process.
